en: The Vow of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, composed by the Great Master Tiantai Zhizhe.
I prostrate to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time. May all Buddhas bear witness to me, [Name]. Whatever [merit] all Buddhas possess...
Regarding all the practices of the *pāramitās*, I shall now likewise train myself accordingly. I pray that all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas will look upon me with compassion and pity.
May I obtain the power of great firmness in the mind of bodhi; may I obtain the power of deep faith in the inconceivable qualities of the Buddhas;
may I obtain the power of non-forgetfulness regarding what I have heard; and [may I attain mastery] over the cycle of birth and death.
In the midst [of practice], he attains the power of tirelessness; among all sentient beings, he attains the power of firm great compassion;
in generosity, he attains the power of firm relinquishment; in ethical discipline, he attains the power of indestructibility; and in patience, he attains the power of firm endurance.
One attains the power of wisdom that Māra cannot destroy, and the power of faith and joy regarding the profound Dharma. First:
"May I, in all places of birth and within all dharmas, always make offerings to all Buddhas of the ten directions, continuing without rest until the end of the future.
Second: "May I receive and uphold the Tathāgata’s ocean of profound Dharma. Immediately—
To attain self-clarification and awakening not through others; to continue without rest until the end of the future;

and third, wherever the Buddhas sit upon the site of enlightenment, to vow to become the foremost leader in gathering the Dharma there, requesting them to turn the wheel of the Dharma to deliver and liberate all sentient beings.
Fourth, may my cultivation of all the boundless and vast vows of all bodhisattvas continue without rest until the end of the future. Fifth, may I teach and transform all sentient beings—
those born from eggs, those born from wombs, those born from moisture, and those born by transformation— and cause them all to enter nirvana without remainder, until the end of the future.
Sixth: May I be born in all Buddha-fields as if they were before my very eyes, until the end of the future, without rest.
Seventh: May I adorn and purify the profound oceans of lands of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
May it continue without rest until the end of the future. Eighth: May I practice together with all bodhisattvas, gathering all roots of goodness without rest until the end of the future. Ninth:
May all the actions of my body, speech, and mind bring benefit to all sentient beings who see or hear them; like the king of medicinal trees, may none pass by in vain until the end of the future.

May there be no cessation throughout the limits of the future. Tenth: May I attain equal and perfect enlightenment within every path of all atoms, turning the great wheel of Dharma and delivering sentient beings, until the end of the future without cessation.
Son of the Buddha, if one can give rise to these ten great vows, then millions of *asaṃkhyeya* gates of vows will all be seen to be brought forth. By means of these vows—

I dedicate these vast vows and various roots of goodness to all sentient beings, wishing that they may forever be free from the sufferings of the three evil realms and fully realize the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

I further dedicate these roots of goodness to unexcelled enlightenment, seeking neither the worldly fruits nor the results of the two vehicles. I further dedicate these roots of goodness to the Truth...
Just as the ocean of the dharma-realm is such that true thusness is without cessation, untainted, unconditioned, and indestructible, may my roots of goodness likewise be so.
Just as the Buddhas of the three periods of time dedicate their merit, I too dedicate in this same way.
Having dedicated, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
